adjudicator: root research investigator; separate mathematical review by production_guards

ours.value: Admissible subsets identify the same population parameter under the stated calibrated Gaussian ACE assumptions. Two admissible subsets can give opposite finite likelihood orderings of the same two ACE parameter points.

claims.methods: Marginalization and the previously reviewed observed-item identification argument, followed by a finite-response-space KL argument. An exact positive-probability response configuration yields opposite fixed-parameter likelihood orderings by Gaussian covariance differentiation. Independent mathematical review verified the explicit calibration, local independence, positivity and joint-support hypotheses.
claims.uncertainty: No statistical interval applies to the conditional written argument. Exact rational covariance identities and strict derivative signs establish the stated restricted comparison; empirical assumptions and broader models are not validated by it.
claims.multiplicity: No sampling hypothesis tests or multiplicity family; this is a restricted analytical implication and constructed example.
claims.status_reason: A conditional Gaussian population-target version is supported by an independently reviewed ordinary argument. Literal finite-likelihood invariance does not follow. This does not assert that the dissertation intended exact finite-sample equality, and does not settle its non-Gaussian latent-genetic interaction models.
claims.numerical: No rounded numerical source effect exists for this proposition; exact covariance identities are computational checks, not a source numerical-agreement claim.
claims.reconstruction_scope: Conditional population identification and a finite-likelihood example on a common calibrated item scale; no empirical refit, opposite-global-MLE claim, significance reversal or formal certificate.
claims.reproduction_deviation: No single numeric reproduction deviation is meaningful. The source-wide claim is narrowed by explicit population-model and observation assumptions; finite likelihood evidence can depend on the subset even when population identification holds.
limitations: The Chapter2 non-Gaussian latent-genetic interaction family and ordinal/multidimensional extensions are not covered.
Actual empirical calibration, conditional independence, joint observation/support and correct specification are not independently verified.
A faithful Lean bridge is absent; this is not a formally certified manuscript theorem.
The finite construction compares two fixed parameter points, not global MLEs or significance decisions.

stopping.reason: The bounded conditional analytical check is complete; the broader source proposition remains partly unresolved.
stopping.attempted: Read the source qualifications at pp5,51,107–108; derive the conditional population/KL bridge; construct both-zygosity, two-moderator-level likelihood witness; independently check exact fractions, derivative signs and assumptions.
stopping.untested: Identification for the Chapter2 non-Gaussian family, broader measurement models, empirical observation/calibration assumptions and faithful formalization.
stopping.resource_basis: Source reading and exact ordinary/symbolic reasoning; no new model fits or numerical integration. Unperformed analytical/formal extensions are open work, not a hard compute denial.
stopping.next_evidence: A faithful observed-response identification argument for each remaining source model, verified empirical calibration/support, and a complete formal bridge for any formally proved manuscript claim.
